verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents QoS settings designed for non-ideal networks, ranging from TCP-like reliable to UDP-like best-effort, plus predefined sensor-data profiles and topics meant for streaming sensor data or robot status. A long-time user also says teleop comes "for free" if you follow ROS conventions. Beyond that, there is no first-party evidence of a teleoperation tool, live video streaming, or remote control over WAN/internet links; the evidence mostly shows communication primitives. Missing for 10: documented teleop tooling, live video streaming/compression, WAN/NAT traversal for remote robots, latency or responsiveness evidence over real-world networks, and independent hands-on corroboration.
